title: How a Falling Cat Flips Mid-Air (Slow Motion Physics)
description:
A falling cat has nothing to push against. So how does it flip and land on its feet? 🐈

It bends in the middle and twists its front and back halves in opposite directions, tucking one pair of legs and stretching the other. Its total spin stays zero the whole time, and it still turns over. First photographed in 1894, explained with maths in 1969. Kittens start doing it at 3 to 4 weeks old.

Did you think cats spin their tail to turn? Tell us 👇

Sources: Kane & Scher, Int. J. Solids and Structures 5, 663-670 (1969); Marey's 1894 chronophotographs.
